flags.quote: Moving your queen to h7 is a blunder because it puts the opponent in check.
flags.critique: I threw a +245 win into a dead draw and you told me the crime was checking them. Checking is not a blunder. Nd2 develops and keeps the extra material; Qh7+ starts a cheap check parade that goes nowhere. If your because-clause is the definition of check, you are not coaching.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b6 doesn't ease a difficult position because it attacks the king directly.
flags.critique: Same inverted lesson. The check is why the move looks tempting, not why it is bad. I am down material and I am checking the king into a safer square. Qh1 actually pins the knight to the rook. 'Because it attacks the king' is the phrase bank talking, not chess.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but taking the knight on e2 with your d3-bishop puts it where the white king and queen can take and you lose a knight.
flags.critique: I put a bishop on a square covered by king and queen. After they recapture I am down a bishop, not a knight. Name the piece that sits on e2 when they take it. If bishop and knight share a label, every capture lesson in this game is suspect.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e2 with your queen doesn't ease a difficult position because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: You used the reason to take as the reason the take is a mistake. The bishop is hanging; that is why Qxe2 looks right. The miss is bxc5, which wins the other bishop and hits the queen. Do not explain a bad recapture with the capture's upside.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on e8 with your queen puts it at risk of attack from the black king.
flags.critique: The king is adjacent and takes the queen next move. 'At risk of attack' is what you say about a maybe-hanging pawn, not about dropping the queen for a defended rook. Say it: the rook is protected, Kxe8 wins the queen, that is a 600-centipawn hole.

flags.quote: Moving your f5-bishop to g6 is the strongest move because it saves your g6-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop is not on g6 until I put it there. g4 is attacking the bishop on f5; I am running away. Say 'it steps off the pawn's attack.' Saving 'your g6-bishop' is the destination square talking to itself.

flags.quote: Moving your g6-bishop to h7 is the strongest move because it saves your h7-bishop from capture.
flags.critique: Identical joke. h5 hits the bishop on g6; Bh7 tucks it into the corner. There is no h7-bishop until the move lands. Also tagging this with backward_pawn is noise I will start ignoring.

flags.quote: Moving your g4-knight to f2 is the strongest move because it saves your f2-knight from capture.
flags.critique: It is a check. The queen on f5 was looking at g4, so the hop also gets off a hanging square, but you named the destination again and skipped the check. 'Saves your f2-knight' is not a lesson. 'Check, and the knight on g4 was hanging' is.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your b1-knight to d2.
flags.critique: f3 is a kingside self-own: it takes the knight's square, pokes a hole in front of an uncastled king, and makes e3 sad. I do not need a lecture on a backward pawn. Tell me I weakened the king and blocked development. Nd2 is development; say that.

flags.quote: Moving your f1-rook to f2 is a blunder, but moving your a1-rook to a2 would be better.
flags.critique: 269 centipawns, zero because. Their rook is staring at my queen on the e-file and e4xf3 opens that line. Rf2 does not get the queen off the file. If you cannot name the discovered attack I am walking into, the 'Want to look at that?' quip is just a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to f2 is a blunder, but moving your pawn to e4 would be better because it unveils an attack from your bishop on the black pawn.
flags.critique: Another 200-centipawn hole with no problem named. The bishop on b6 already cuts through f2; I parked the queen on that diagonal. e4 is a center break that opens g2 toward d5. Tell me I put the queen on the bishop's laser. 'Unveils an attack on the black pawn' is too cowardly to name d5.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on f3 with your queen is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the black c6-knight.
flags.critique: I recaptured a pawn that just took on f3. That pawn was not defending the knight on c6. Recapture, then stop. Inventing removed-defender on a recapture trains me to hallucinate tactics that are not on the board.

flags.quote: Moving your king to f1 is a blunder, but moving your king to d1 would be better because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: 334 centipawns for 'harder to attack' is phrase-bank fog. After Re8+ the king has two flights. Kf1 walks into Qe3, which sits in the hole and stares at everything. Kd1 steps off that file. Name the queen check. 'Harder to attack' is what you say when you did not look.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your c1-bishop to d2 leaves your pawn hanging to the black h7-bishop.
flags.critique: Third time this game you mention the d3 pawn hanging to that bishop, and this time it is a blunder with no better move. I already missed Bxd3 on move 26. If you are going to cry hanging pawn again, at least show me the move that actually covers d3. A blunder with suggestedMoveSan null is a shrug.

flags.quote: Moving your c6-knight to e5 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The knight hits the queen on f3. That is the whole move. Empty verdict on a queen attack is malpractice. I should hear 'the knight attacks the queen,' not 'that's the one.'

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on e3 with your d2-bishop is the strongest move because the pawn was undefended and you take the defender of the black bishop.
flags.critique: The pawn on e3 just forked my queen and bishop. I am recapturing the forking pawn. It does not defend the bishop on b6. Teach the recapture of a pawn fork, not a fake removed-defender.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is the strongest move because you claim more of the center.
flags.critique: This is Van't Kruijs. e3 is a timid center pawn, not 'the strongest move.' e4 and d4 actually take the middle. Calling 1.e3 strongest because center is how you get a 1200 to believe a second-rate opening is theory.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on e3 with your queen is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended and then pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: The pin is real: queen on e3 nails e5 to the rook on e8. The sentence is not. 'And then pin' has no subject. I should not have to parse a template join to get a real tactic.

flags.quote: You are still winning, but moving your queen to c6 leaves your e5-knight hanging to the white queen. A better move would have been moving your f2-knight to d3 because it saves your d3-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The hang is the right lesson: Qf5 takes the knight on e5. Then you ruin it with destination-saves again. Nfd3 saves the knight that is on f2, not a d3-knight that does not exist yet. Also ignored_threat is listed twice, which is how I know this is a machine.

flags.quote: Moving your d2-bishop to c1 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: The bishop was sitting between the queen on d1 and the hanging pawn on d3. Sliding to c1 lets the queen guard d3. You never said that. 'Saves your pawn' without naming the unblocked queen is a riddle, not a lesson.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: You kick the bishop on f5. That is the only idea, and the eval even dips. Empty 'strongest' plus 'That's the one.' on a 52-centipawn swing is you refusing to say pawn-attacks-bishop.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to d4 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: This is the central break the last five moves were begging for. It cracks e3 and sets the pawn fork. Blank verdict on the thematic pawn push is how a coach admits it only talks when a detector fires.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your f1-bishop to g2 leaves your pawn hanging to the black g6-bishop.
flags.critique: You already said this on Ne2. Same bishop, same d3 pawn, same shrug. I got it. If the pawn is still hanging, stop fianchettoing and cover it. Repeating the hang line without a new idea is nagging.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The only reason tag is backward_pawn, and you did not even print it. c3 supports a later d4 and is a slow setup pawn. 'Strongest' with a silent structural tag is template residue. Either teach the d4 plan or stop calling it strongest.

flags.quote: Moving your queen to f5 is the strongest move because it saves your queen from capture.
flags.critique: The save is true: Ne5 was hitting the queen. Then the eval drops 143 centipawns and you still stamp strongest. Saving a hanging queen onto a worse square is damage control, not a brilliancy. Call it the only way to keep the queen, not the strongest move in the game.

suggestions.title: Never explain a blunder as 'because it checks'
suggestions.detail: select-insight treats concept 'check' as explainPlayedAsBenefit, so Qh7+ and Qb6+ get phrase-bank check lines as the because of a blunder. Drop check from benefit-explanation when classification is inaccuracy/mistake/blunder, and never let a check phrase be the sole because of a bad move. A 1200 will remember 'checking is a blunder' and stop checking forever.

suggestions.title: Stop saving the destination square
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses the moved unit after it lands, so Bg6 'saves your g6-bishop', Bh7 'saves your h7-bishop', Nf2+ 'saves your f2-knight', Nfd3 'saves your d3-knight'. Name the piece on the from-square or as 'your bishop/knight', and add saves_piece to dropTautologyReasons when piece.square === move.to. This fired four times in one game.

suggestions.title: Label the piece you actually hung
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 250+ to 'a knight', so a hanging bishop (330) becomes 'you lose a knight' on Bxe2. hangingLossCopy returns null above 400, so a hanging queen on Qxe8+ becomes 'at risk of attack' instead of 'you lose a queen'. Split bishop/knight bands by piece type, and do not null out rook/queen losses. Wrong piece names destroy trust.

suggestions.title: Do not praise the capture you just called a mistake
suggestions.detail: concept 'capture' is in explainPlayedAsBenefit, so Qxe2 (mistake vs bxc5) renders as 'doesn't ease a difficult position because the bishop was undefended'. When the played capture is not the best move, use problem/contrast reasons, not wins_material. The because should be why the other capture was better, not why this one took a free piece.

suggestions.title: Kill removed-defender on recaptures
suggestions.detail: Bxe3 'takes the defender of the black bishop' and Qxf3 'takes the defender of the c6-knight' are both recaptures of a pawn that does not defend those pieces. Gate removed_defender unless the newly hanging unit is actually hanging after the move. 1200s will start seeing ghosts on every recapture.

suggestions.title: Prefer king-safety over backward-pawn on f-pawn lunges
suggestions.detail: f3, c3, g3, e5, Bh7 all carry backward_pawn, and f3's problem line is 'creates a backward pawn to defend' while the real cost is king holes and blocking Ng1. Rank pawn_shield / king_more_exposed / development above backward_pawn unless the backward pawn is the actual hanging weakness. Structure tags are drowning the opening.

suggestions.title: Never ship a blunder with no suggestion
suggestions.detail: Bd2 (ply 31, 218cp) has suggestedMoveSan null. If bestMoveUci exists, always surface it on mistake/blunder. A hanging-pawn lecture without the covering move is just scolding. Pair with a rule: if benefit reasons are empty, do not emit a bare 'strongest move' on Ne5, d4, g4, c3.

suggestions.title: If a move hits a queen or kicks a bishop, say so
suggestions.detail: Ne5 attacks Qf3 and still prints an empty strongest-move line. g4 kicks Bf5 the same way. Add a 'attacks_piece' / 'kicks_piece' fact when the moved unit newly attacks a higher-value piece, and let discourse prefer that over silence. Empty 'That's the one.' on queen attacks is the aesthetic that makes the whole dump feel like a template farm.

whatWorked: Castling copy on 16 and 39 actually names king safety and the rook.
Qd6 missed Bxd3 because the pawn was undefended — the first time d3 hanging became a real takeaway, and Bxd3 later paid it off.
dxe3 named the pawn fork of bishop and queen, then the discovered queen hit on d2.
Bxe3 (black) named the pin of queen to king on the diagonal.
exf3 named the discovered rook hitting the queen on the e-file.
Qc6+ correctly said the e5-knight hangs to the queen (before the destination-save ruined the suggestion).
Qh8+ actually said skewer, king in front of rook.
Ke7 named the discovered rook hitting the queen — the right way to meet the skewer.
Qxd3+ named the fork of king and knight; Qxc3 named the pin of knight to king.
